correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the proof for invariant Lebesgue measure and the centered logarithm, whose lag-zero variance is 1. Branch substitution x=(j+t)/q gives the logarithm of the gamma product; integrating the alternating power series for log(1+t) against log t gives C_1=1−pi²/24. Strictly decreasing branch average and −log t have strictly positive covariance. The positive Stirling remainder and 0≤t≤1 give a uniform bound |R_q(t)|≤1/q, so integration gives the claimed q⁻² bound. The stationarity tail is 2 sum_{j≥1} j C_{N+j}; geometric sums give the stated correction and (8/9)4⁻ᴺ error, including N=1. The Q_K bound uses the unweighted geometric tail. In a fresh, separate 40-decimal replay, independent branch quadrature and the gamma expression agreed through q=16, direct finite-sum integration agreed for N=1 through 4, c and C_1 agreed with the stated approximations, and K=16 tail enclosures for the variance rate and intercept were compatible with their displayed decimals.
